subject: Cloud Computing
title: The Cost of Storing Everything
description: A fast breakdown of The Cost of Storing Everything for builders.

hook.text: A company stores 10 petabytes of data 'just in case.' Annual cost: $250,000. Nobody has queried most of it in years.

buildup.text: Cloud storage is cheap per gigabyte. But at scale, keeping everything adds up to significant ongoing expense.

discovery.text: Data retention policies define what to keep, for how long, and when to delete. Compliance often dictates minimums.

twist.text: Deleting data is emotionally hard. Teams hoard data because 'we might need it someday.' Someday rarely comes.

climax.text: The discipline of data lifecycle management separates cost-efficient teams from those drowning in unused storage.

punchline.text: Just because you can store everything doesn't mean you should.

quiz.question: Why do many teams struggle with cloud storage costs?
options: They hoard data indefinitely instead of implementing retention policies
Cloud storage prices increase every year by 50%
Data cannot be deleted once stored in the cloud

details.summary: Many organizations store data indefinitely because cloud storage seems cheap per gigabyte. But at petabyte scale, storage costs mount to millions annually. Egress fees, API calls, and compliance overhead add hidden costs on top of raw storage pricing.
details.whyItMatters: Storing everything forever is a hidden budget drain. Rational data retention policies save money and reduce compliance risk from holding sensitive data longer than necessary.
takeaways: Per-gigabyte costs seem low but scale to millions at volume
Egress and API call fees add significantly to storage costs
Data retention policies are essential for cost and compliance

faq.question: What are egress fees?
faq.answer: Egress fees are charges for transferring data out of a cloud provider's network. Ingress is usually free, but downloading or moving data to another provider or the internet incurs per-gigabyte charges that can be surprisingly large at scale.

faq.question: How do you build a data retention policy?
faq.answer: Classify data by type and sensitivity. Define retention periods based on legal, regulatory, and business requirements. Automate deletion or archival at the end of each period. Review and update policies annually as requirements change.
